- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

I made a pixel-art Eiffel Tower in `./output/eiffel_tower_16color.jpg` (512×512, about 132 KB).

I read "16-bit color" as a retro look built from a 16-colour palette, not a 16-bit file format. JPG stores 8 bits per channel, so the limit is in the artwork itself. The image is drawn on a 128×128 pixel grid and scaled up 4× with sharp pixel edges. The sky is dithered between palette colours, and the tower has a diagonal lattice, two platforms, the arch and the antenna. There is also a sun and three clouds.

The generator script, `./output/make_eiffel.py`, is included as the source. It writes no intermediate files, and I reviewed the rendered image to check the result.
